why_hn: Used as a vivid example of spinal pattern generators and morphological control in locomotion discussions.

title: The Prodigy - Firestarter (Official Video)
summary: The official music video for Firestarter by The Prodigy, the 1990s electronic hit featuring Keith Flint.
why_hn: HN mentions it mainly as nostalgia, a tribute to Keith Flint, or a throwaway joke rather than as a recommendation.

title: RTTY DEMO 012710.wmv
summary: A short demonstration of radioteletype (RTTY), a digital communication mode used in amateur radio, showing what the signal sounds like.
why_hn: HN commenters link it as a sound sample when discussing data-over-audio projects that resemble RTTY.

title: "Computer Says No..." | Little Britain | Lucas & Walliams
summary: The Little Britain sketch in which call-center worker Carol types into her computer and replies 'computer says no' to every request.
why_hn: HN uses it as a joke reference to automated systems and bureaucratic refusals.

title: Why We Should NOT Look For Aliens - The Dark Forest
summary: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on the Dark Forest answer to the Fermi Paradox. It argues that if advanced civilizations exist, staying silent may be the safest strategy because revealing yourself invites a first strike.
why_hn: HN commenters cite it as the accessible summary of the Dark Forest theory whenever SETI, alien contact, or hostile-environment analogies come up.

title: The Wire: Fix The Crime Statistics...or...
summary: A two-minute scene from The Wire in which Baltimore police brass pressure subordinates to fix the crime statistics. It dramatizes how metrics and incentives distort policing.
why_hn: Used as a shorthand illustration of juking the stats and Goodhart-style metric gaming.

title: Cadillac ELR Coupe 2014 Commercial
summary: A short, ironic Cadillac ELR 2014 commercial celebrating long working hours and the American dream, which has been widely mocked.
why_hn: Cited critically as an example of US advertising that glorifies overwork and lack of holiday time.

title: The Simpsons Anti-Tiger Rock
summary: A one-minute clip from The Simpsons in which Lisa demonstrates the Anti-Tiger Rock to Homer, showing that the rock keeps away tigers because no tigers are around. It is a short comedic scene about faulty causal reasoning.
why_hn: HN commenters post it as a joke whenever a thread involves correlation, causation, or unfalsifiable protective measures.

title: 9/10/2001: Rumsfeld says $2.3 TRILLION Missing from Pentagon
summary: Short clip of Donald Rumsfeld's 9/10/2001 speech acknowledging that $2.3 trillion in Pentagon transactions could not be tracked.
why_hn: Referenced when commenters discuss unaccounted government money, conspiracy theories, or financial fraud.

title: Which Penetrating Oil is Best? Let's find out!
summary: Project Farm tests six penetrating oils, including WD-40, PB Blaster, Liquid Wrench and an ATF and acetone mix, on rusted bolts. Liquid Wrench placed first and the homemade mix second.
why_hn: Cited as a hands-on comparison showing WD-40 is not the best penetrating oil.

title: The Big Short (2015) - Jared Vennett's Pitch to Front Point Partners (Jenga Blocks Scene) [HD 1080p]
summary: A scene from The Big Short in which Jared Vennett pitches credit default swaps on mortgage bonds to a hedge fund team, using a Jenga tower to illustrate collateralized debt obligations.
why_hn: Used as a quick visual explanation of how CDOs packaged risky mortgage debt.

title: 1 -  L'énergie - Cours des Mines 2019 - Jancovici -  [EN subtitles available]
summary: Part 1 of Jean-Marc Jancovici's 2019 course at Ecole des Mines de Paris, on energy and its central role in the economy and climate. It is in French with English subtitles available and runs about two and a half hours.
why_hn: Cited as a source lecture series behind arguments on energy, EROEI, nuclear power and climate.

title: So you think you can validate email addresses A journey down RFC5321
summary: Stavros Korokithakis gives a FOSDEM 2018 talk on how hard it is to validate email addresses properly, taking a tour through RFC 5321.
why_hn: Linked whenever email validation comes up as a fun illustration of how deceptively difficult it is.

title: ESCAPE FROM NEW YORK : SNAKE PLISSKEN FLIGHT ON TWIN TOWERS
summary: A scene from John Carpenter's 1981 film Escape from New York in which Snake Plissken glides in over Manhattan between the Twin Towers. It features the film's wireframe green laser-grid visuals built from miniatures.
why_hn: HN uses it to illustrate how the film's wireframe skyline effect was made with practical miniatures and as an example of retro computer-display aesthetics.

title: The Wire: Chicken McNuggets
summary: A two-minute clip from The Wire in which characters speculate about who invented Chicken McNuggets.
why_hn: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about accidental inventors and automating jobs.

title: UNBELTED Passenger in Frontal Car Crash
summary: IIHS frontal crash test footage showing what happens to an unbelted rear-seat passenger. It illustrates that buckling up in the back matters for the passenger and for front occupants.
why_hn: Used as a visual example in seat belt and personal-freedom debates, showing an unbelted rear passenger becoming a projectile.

title: Don't Mention the War! | Fawlty Towers | BBC Comedy Greats
summary: The classic Fawlty Towers scene in which Basil Fawlty tries not to mention the war while serving German guests, ending in goose-stepping and mocking. It is a two-minute BBC comedy clip with John Cleese.
why_hn: HN mentions it mainly as a joke reference or as an example of humor that many Germans reportedly find funny.

title: Tom Lehrer - Poisoning Pigeons In The Park
summary: Tom Lehrer performs his satirical song about poisoning pigeons in the park, in a rare 1967 Norwegian broadcast recording.
why_hn: Posted as a humorous reference in threads about pigeons or Lehrer.

title: 9/11: A Conspiracy Theory
summary: James Corbett's five-minute conspiracy-framed overview of 9/11 claims.
why_hn: Rarely discussed in substance; mentions are bare links in unrelated threads.

title: Everything About Grain Bins (Farmers are Geniuses) - Smarter Every Day 218
summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explores how grain bins work and the engineering and know-how involved in farming. His point is that farmers are exceptionally capable.
why_hn: Used as supporting evidence in threads on farming that farmers are smart, skilled and quantitative.

title: why Japan's internet is weirdly designed
summary: Answer in Progress investigates why Japanese websites look different from those elsewhere, using an AI clustering approach to test the 2013 claim. It then looks at possible explanations.
why_hn: Cited as a companion to articles on Japanese web design and as an example of clustering websites by appearance.

title: WORLD RECORD SPEED TEST
summary: An Opera browser promotional video from 2010 in which a browser races a potato in a tongue-in-cheek speed test.
why_hn: Mostly brought up ironically, as a remembered ad or joke when browser speed claims come up.

title: China - 3,000 Years of History in a Minute
summary: An animated map of the territories of Chinese dynasties from 1000 BC to the present, compressed into about a minute.
why_hn: Cited in passing to show how China's borders have expanded and contracted over history.

title: How to Create a Mind | Ray Kurzweil | Talks at Google
summary: Ray Kurzweil presents his book How to Create a Mind at Google, on reverse engineering the brain and using that understanding to build intelligent machines. He shows his graphs of exponential technological progress.
why_hn: Linked in threads about Kurzweil joining Google, mostly as a source for his exponential progress charts and his ambitions there.

title: British Army on LSD (Acid) drugs
summary: Archive footage from 1964 of Royal Marine Commando volunteers filmed on a field exercise after taking LSD at Porton Down. It documents a British military drug trial.
why_hn: HN cites it as evidence for strange military experiments, in particular soldiers being dosed with LSD to test their performance.

title: Nanofactory Animation
summary: A short animation illustrating the proposed nanofactory concept, where nanomachines assemble atomically precise parts into larger products. It depicts how such a system might build macroscopic goods from raw materials and energy.
why_hn: Shared as a visualization of Ralph Merkle's theoretical work on molecular manufacturing.
